title: Why Do Dogs Violently Shake Their Toys?
description:

script: Your dog is trying to kill that toy. Literally. That violent side to side shake is a hunting move passed down from wild ancestors, the exact motion used to snap the neck of small prey after catching it, built straight into their neurology. Your dog isn't hunting a real animal with a squeaky toy, but that instinct never disappeared, it just gets redirected onto whatever's available. That's actually why the squeak matters so much, it mimics the sound small prey would make, which triggers and rewards that same predatory sequence. Completely normal, deeply satisfying play.
